title: Executable Runbook (Lite) for Rookie On-call: Runbook-as-Task UX and Safe Adminlets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight 'executable runbook' experience aimed at junior/on-call engineers with minimal product knowledge. The goal is a safe, discoverable runbook-as-task surface that turns playbooks into typed, audited tasks (adminlets) with built-in dry-run, permission gates, and automatic telemetry. This is a scoped, beta 'Lite' feature that avoids full runbook DSL complexity while delivering measurable TTR reductions for common incidents.
background: On-call rotations show repeated low-complexity incidents where junior engineers hesitate to run scripts or escalate due to fear of side effects. Existing runbook tooling is powerful but heavy: complex DSLs, many parameters, and limited safety nets. We need a 'lite' path: convert safe operational steps into short, validated tasks with explicit inputs, a sandbox/dry-run, and mandatory confirmation + audit trail.
goals: Reduce mean time to mitigation (TTR) for 10 highest-frequency low-risk incident types by 30% for junior engineers
Provide audited adminlet execution with minimal cognitive overhead
Ship a minimal UX that can be expanded to full runbook-as-code later
acceptance_criteria: Product UI: runbook task view that shows step summary, typed inputs, preconditions, and risk level
Safety: every adminlet requires at least one confirmation and performs a dry-run simulation showing expected changes
RBAC: executions are gated to roles; audit log entry created for every run (user, params, result)
Telemetry: events emitted for start/complete/failure with tags (runbook_id, step_id, user_role)
E2E: three sample on-call runbooks converted and validated in staging; demo runbook executed by engineer in staging without infra side effects
implementation_notes: Architectural approach: runbook authoring -> compile to 'task manifest' (YAML) containing typed inputs, validators, dry-run generator, and a gated exec wrapper
Execution surface: small React web component inside Console + lightweight CLI shim for terminal users
Safety stack: dry-run + precondition checks -> confirmation modal with human-readable diff -> guarded execution under a short-lived privileged token
Audit: write events to existing audit pipeline (https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/doc/runbook-exec) and attach trace id to request
Telemetry: use existing telemetry schema ops.runbook.exec.{start, dryrun, confirm, result}
milestones: 2025-02-20: Spec drafted and design sketch reviewed by PM/Design
2025-02-26: Prototype web component + CLI shim implemented (alpha)
2025-03-10: Staging conversion of three canonical runbooks and on-call dry-runs
2025-03-15: Beta rollout gate and docs for SRE/on-call rotation
risks: Overconfidence: 'lite' surface may encourage running tasks without full understanding; mitigated by strong dry-run and prominent risk labels
Privilege escalation: short-lived tokens need strict scoping and automated revocation
Complexity creep: feature might grow into full DSL if not strictly scoped; enforce MVP boundaries
Operational load: support team may see increased runbook executions requiring monitoring of demand and cost
open_questions: What is the minimal validation set for typed inputs? (regex vs schema)
Should dry-run be deterministic or best-effort when external state changes?
How to represent multi-step transactions where partial failure requires rollback?
What role granularity for RBAC (team-level vs capability-level)?
test_plan: Unit: validator logic for typed inputs and dry-run generator
Integration: end-to-end runbook conversion -> staging exec with mock infra (no side effects)
Chaos: simulate state drift between dry-run and execute path and verify detection/abort
User test: on-call shadowing session where junior engineer follows the runbook and we collect usability feedback
rollout_plan: Internal beta: SRE + two product teams on staging for 2 weeks
Canary: enable for 10% of on-call rotations with telemetry monitoring
Full beta: enable for all on-call after 4 successful canary days and no P1 regressions
Docs: publish quickstart + FAQ, and a template repo for authors
